# Rule quality matrix

Generated by `skillguard gold matrix --gold research/gold/HUMAN-v1.jsonl --all-rules
--format markdown`. Do not edit the table by hand; regenerate it.

**Every rule is `INFORMATIONAL` and every recall is `unknown`, because no human has
labelled anything yet.** That is the honest state, not an unfinished table: the
`GOLD-v1`..`GOLD-v10` sets in `research/gold/` are **model** labels, and two
models agreeing is not a human label (`docs/GOLD_EVALUATION.md` §1).

| | |
|---|---|
| dataset | `research/gold/HUMAN-v1.jsonl` — empty |
| worksheet | `research/gold/HUMAN-v1.worksheet.csv` — 95 rows, awaiting a reviewer |
| rule set | `skillguard 0.1.2`, `SCAN_LOGIC_REVISION = 53` |
| thresholds | Blocking ≥ 95% on ≥ 30 samples; Warning ≥ 85% on ≥ 20 (`src/gold.rs`) |

To fill it: `docs/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md`, about 40 minutes for 95 rows. Then:

```bash
skillguard gold import research/gold/HUMAN-v1.worksheet.csv \
    --out research/gold/HUMAN-v1.jsonl
skillguard gold matrix --gold research/gold/HUMAN-v1.jsonl --all-rules \
    --format markdown > docs/RULE_QUALITY_MATRIX.md
```

**Recall is `unknown` for every rule and will stay unknown here.** A finding-level
sample is drawn from findings, so the rules' misses are absent by construction.
Measuring recall needs a skill-level sample ("did this skill contain this
behaviour at all?"), which is a different instrument and a different round.
Synthetic fixtures are never presented as corpus recall.
